Ruling: batch #132 item 3 · letter B · maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-13T12:4xZ (to `1A·2(2)·3B·4是`)

## Ruling recorded — B: the by-name app probe distinguishes "not found" from "unreachable" — two answers the transport already gives — and the screen says only what was measured, with A's wording as the not-found copy (director seat, decision batch #132 item 3, 2026-09-13)

Derived first from the long-term axis: a screen states what it measured, never what it guesses — the rule #4252 already applied to this screen once. The information B needs is already on the wire (404 vs 5xx / offline / timeout), folded into one `unknown` by `probeAppAccess`; distinguishing transport failure from not-found does not widen the enumeration surface the 2026-08-12 ruling guarded (the control plane still answers 404 for every app the caller may not see). C would keep a screen asserting an unmeasured state. ②③④ do not overturn ①; the seat's "A now, B later" is not taken — one delivery.

### What is ruled
1. `ObjectStackDataSource.probeAppAccess` returns `granted | denied | not_found | unreachable` (`unknown` only for a host DataSource that cannot answer — cause 5). `Clause-②: yes` (a published DataSource contract widens by two members).
2. `AppContent.tsx` copy by verdict: `not_found` ⇒ "This app can't be opened" (no cause asserted) + Retry; `unreachable` ⇒ "Couldn't reach the server" + Retry; `denied` unchanged (#4252); `unknown` ⇒ the neutral copy. The "it may still be publishing" sentence is retired; a genuine post-publish lag reads as `not_found` and the one forced `refreshMetadata()` stays.
3. Acceptance step one: measure cause 8 (probe `granted` while the list still lacks the app) on a real registry lag before the new branches land — it is the shape the new branches would otherwise miss.
4. Ten locale tables updated (the i18n seat's own review applies).

### State
`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `bug` / `domain:ui` / `priority:p2` kept; cross-package face (`data-objectstack`, `app-shell`, `i18n`) declared in the claim.

## ACCEPT — PR objectui#9411 · reviewed against GitHub, ⛔ not against the report

`domain:ui` seat, R3, 2026-09-13T16:5xZ. **Form**: draft, base `main`, `Fixes #9262` first line, 18 files `+609/-110`, governed hits **0**, all 9 required checks green.

### ⭐ The headline: ruling item 3 paid for itself, and it changed the implementation

The ruling ordered cause 8 measured **before the new branches land**. The dev booted a real objectstack server and measured — and **falsified the card's own premise**:

| probe | before the fix | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `showcase_app` (exists) | `granted`, in list | `granted` |
| `no_such_app_xyz` | **`granted`**, http **200** | `not_found` |
| `zzz_typo_9262` | **`granted`**, http **200** | `not_found` |
| `finance` (unpublished) | **`granted`**, http **200** | `not_found` |

⇒ **the by-name route does NOT answer 404 for an absent app.** It answers **200 carrying the declared envelope minus its `item`**, because in `rest-server.ts` both the 403 and the 404 sit inside `if (isAppType && visible)` — and for a name resolving to nothing, `visible` is undefined, so the gate is skipped entirely. The 404 branch is reachable **only** for an app that exists and is withheld for a non-permission reason.

⭐ **Why this is the whole card**: a `not_found` keyed on the status code — the obvious reading of the ruling, and the reading **my own ZONE 3 nudged toward** — would have been **dead for every typo and every unpublished draft**, and every local gate would have been green. Verified in the diff that it was not built that way: `:5828` reads `metaEnvelopeCarriesItem(envelope) ? 'granted' : 'not_found'`, absence taken from the **envelope** as well as the code.

### Other spot checks

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| ten locale packs | **exactly 10** in the diff (ar de en es fr ja ko pt ru zh) — matches the ruling's word, counted from the PR's file list |
| existing pin | `AppContent.deniedVsUnpublished.test.tsx` **rewritten, ⛔ not deleted**; its four "MUST NOT CHANGE — keeps the publishing copy" cases became per-verdict screens |
| enumeration surface | ⛔ not widened — nothing new is read off the list, so the 2026-08-12 ruling's guard holds |
| ablation | mutation proved on disk before running; exactly 3 cases went red, all three being the measured-absence rows. ⭐ **Cross-package leg**: the union was narrowed in the **built declaration** `app-shell` actually resolves, turning its type-check red at exactly three consuming sites — proving the consumer reads that file and not a cache |
| ⭐ honest self-report | the dev flagged that its **producer-side ablation guard was VACUOUS** (the build had failed, so `dist` did not exist and the grep guard could not fire), noticed it, and ran a separate clean leg instead. Reporting a vacuous guard rather than letting it stand as proof is the behaviour I most want to see |

### Deviations — all acceptable

Booted a real server with two dependency-closure builds (worktrees removed, server stopped by verified PID, port confirmed closed); the `--pair N` script my protocol names **does not exist in objectui** and was reported rather than fabricated; repo-wide lint/test left to CI with a stated invariance argument (no type-aware linting is configured, proven with a positive control, so this diff cannot move a file it does not contain).

⚠️ **One judgement the dev surfaced instead of taking silently**: `granted` reaching the missing-app branch is cause 8 itself and is **not assigned copy by the ruling**. It was routed to the neutral screen with the reason in code and PR. ⇒ correct handling; if a distinct screen for a live registry disagreement is wanted, that is a follow-up, ⛔ not something this PR should have invented.

**Out-of-scope finding**: `objectstack-ai/objectstack#18066` filed for the server-side shape (a 200 with an item-less envelope where `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` declares `item` **required**). Filed bare in the **fix-landing repo**, ⛔ ungraded — correct, grading is triage's. Its dedupe carried a known-must-hit control that fired, so its zero is a reading.

Clause-② in-seat review is **PASS** (recorded on the PR); carriers stripped, then ready + auto-merge.
